full_judgment:
Md Abdur Rashid J: Defendant No. 1 presented the appeal against the decree dated 30-6-2002 passed by the Joint District Judge, Court No. 4 at Dhaka in Title Suit No. 204 of 1999, which decreed the suit for ejectment. 

 10. Upon the evidence, oral and documentary, on record learned Joint District Judge decreed the suit and asked defendant No. 1 to vacate the suit premises within 60 days from date. He also granted a decree for Taka 13,16,360 as 11 months' arrears from 1-10-1998 to 31-8-1999 and payment of future rents from September 1999 at the rate of Taka 1,28,760 with interest at bank rate till eviction. 

 11. On behalf of the appellant the decree was challenged mainly on the ground that the learned Joint District Judge erred in law in decreeing the suit in the absence of valid termination of tenancy by a valid notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act. In support, Abdul Aziz vs Md Abdul Majid, 2 BLT (AD) 151 and Abdul Noor and others vs Mohammood Ali and others, 54 DLR (AD) 67 were cited. 

 22. Section 18 of the Premises Rent Control Act, 1991 provides, inter alia, that notwithstanding anything contained in the Transfer of Property Act or the Contract Act no order or decree for the recovery of possession of any premises shall be made as long as the tenant pays rent to the full extent allowable by the Act and performs other conditions of the tenancy. 

 23. It is therefore, now settled that expiry of the lease would not ipso facto entitle a lessor to a decree for eviction of a tenant so long the tenant pays rent and complies with other terms of the contract. In the case before us, defendant No. 1 admittedly stopped paying rent since October, 1998. He did not take any step to pay rent since then. So, the defendant became a defaulter. Ultimately, he was evicted through process of the Court on 16-8-2003. The arrears piled up to Taka 13,16,360 from 1-10-1998 to 31-8-1999 before he was evicted. The decree passed therefore, cannot be said to be invalid. 

 30. In the circumstances, judgment and decree of the trial Court do not suffer from any illegality or irregularity. The appeal fails, accordingly. 

 31. Before parting, we must say that after eviction of defendant No. 1 the decree for arrear rent for the period from October, 1998 to August, 1999 for eleven months would be sufficient to meet justice in the facts and circumstances of the case. 

 32. Result being the appeal is dismissed with cost. Judgment and decree for eviction of defendant No. 1 and payment of Taka 13,16,360 as arrears of 11 months from 1-10-1998 to 30-9-1999 are hereby affirmed and the rest of the decree is set aside.
